title: Israel’s Message to a Broad Swath of Lebanon: Shiites Must Go
partialText: Israel has issued sweeping evacuation warnings, and pressed some Christian and Druse leaders to expel Shiite Muslims from southern towns, the leaders said.

title: Trump Says Europe Is On Its Own in Securing the Strait of Hormuz
partialText: Threatening to pull out of NATO, President Trump portrayed the alliance as a “paper tiger” and said Europe was on its own in trying to secure the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Placing U.S. Troops in Middle East Hotels May Violate Laws of War
partialText: U.S. commanders have kept many troops away from bases in the region to protect them from Iran’s ballistic missile attacks.

title: C.D.C. Pauses Testing for Rabies and Mpox
partialText: The diseases were removed from a list of tests the agency conducts for state and local health departments. Experts worry that with drastic staff reductions, the testing may not resume.

title: U.S. Plans Military Expansion in Greenland
partialText: The Pentagon is in talks with Denmark for access to three more areas on the Arctic island. Several Greenlanders said they didn’t like the idea.

title: How to Watch NASA’s Artemis II Moon Launch Online
partialText: NASA will broadcast the launch of the Artemis II mission as well as holding live conversations with the crew during their time in space.

title: Why the Artemis II Astronauts Will Be Wearing Orange
partialText: It’s not just any orange. It’s International Orange.

title: Memphis House Primary Exemplifies Democrats’ Age Fights
partialText: A primary in Tennessee between Representative Steve Cohen, a white incumbent, and Justin Pearson, a Black state lawmaker, exemplifies a national push for a passing of the torch.

title: South Dakotans React to Daily Mail Article on Bryon Noem, Kristi Noem’s Husband
partialText: In the tiny town of Castlewood, S.D., where everyone knows the Noems, the prevailing sense was that people can’t help but feel bad for Bryon Noem after a tabloid photo leak.

title: Who Murdered Minerliz? How a Diner Meet-up Cracked the Case.
partialText: In 1999, a 13-year-old girl was found dead in the Bronx. Then the trail went cold for 20 years, until an ingenious ploy by detectives produced a vital clue to her killer.

title: One of Apple’s First Employees Looks Back at 50 Years
partialText: In 1976, 14-year-old Chris Espinosa rode a moped to his job demonstrating computers made in Steve Jobs’s childhood home. The company has changed a bit since then.

title: Bruce Springsteen Brings Fiery Speeches and Songs to Minneapolis
partialText: The E Street Band opened its Land of Hope and Dreams tour on Tuesday night, where the musician asked the crowd to choose “unity over division and peace over war.”

title: Tech Bros Hacked Their Diets. Now You May Be Doing It, Too.
partialText: With seeds, supplements and gadgets (but little expert guidance), Americans of all stripes are seeking wellness through what they eat.

title: Trump’s War Is Perpetually ‘Ahead of Schedule'
partialText: In Iran, the schedule is our most malleable illusion.

title: Padma Lakshmi: The Decision That Would Create a Permanent American Underclass
partialText: Trump wants to take away a fundamental American promise.

title: Born American
partialText: We look at an important case before the Supreme Court.

title: In New England, Catching Climate Data Along With Fish
partialText: Commercial vessels are deploying high-tech sensors to map a shifting sea, providing critical data for scientists and some help for the industry.

title: A ‘Traffic Jam’ of Trials Poses Headache for Mangione’s Lawyers
partialText: Luigi Mangione’s lawyers could be in and out of court in Manhattan through the end of the year. A judge could decide as early as Wednesday on whether to delay his federal case.

title: When Racism Is a Crime: Brazil Puts a Tourist on Trial for Word and Gesture
partialText: An Argentine woman, who is white, could face years in prison after being accused of racism. The case has set off intense debate in Argentina and Brazil.
